newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico peso ends firm on long bond, primary hopes.
newsitem.headline: Mexico peso ends firm on long bond, primary hopes.

text.p: The Mexican peso reversed earlier weakness to close firm across the board due to a decline in U.S. long bond rates and forecast increases in local primary rates, traders said.
"The market overbought dollars in the morning, ahead of Greenspan's speech, but those dollars came back when the international markets settled down," a trader said.
The benchmark 48-hour peso and its 24-hour stablemate closed 0.35 and 0.4 of a centavo firmer, respectively, at 7.7965/7.7995 and 7.7910/7.7960 per dollar.
Same-day peso contracts closed earlier 1.6 centavos firmer at 7.7940/7.7980 per dollar.

Traders said yields on 30-year U.S. Treasury bonds gained to 6.89 percent in early trade, from 6.83 percent on Monday, ahead of testimony provided by U.S. Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan to the Senate Budget Committee.

Greenspan said nothing to compare with his "irrational exhuberance" comments of early December, which unsettled international markets, and long bond yields fell to 6.78 percent in late trade, which traders said helped shore up the peso.

Money market traders surveyed by Reuters meanwhile forecast an average rise of five basis points in bellwether 28-day Cetes (Treasury Certificates) to 23.03 percent at Tuesday night's primary auction.
